segs.t: Préserver et faire rayonner le patrimoine culturel et artistique des communautés noires en misant sur l’innovation et l'échange interculturel.
To preserve the cultural and artistic heritage of Black communities and make it shine, through innovation and intercultural exchange. — CCAM mission, English rendering by the studio

These guidelines cover CCAM’s 2026 season: the Black History Month calendar, the three-part conference series at Campus MIL, and the Chantier exhibition at Galerie Art Mûr.

They describe the season as it has been designed. Every measurement comes from the season’s Instagram posts and posters. Where a rule had to be written rather than measured, it is marked as recommended.

They are for anyone making season material: CCAM staff, partners, venues and printers. Use them to add new posts, posters or screens that sit with what already exists.

The CCAM logo has its own rules. This book only covers how the logo is used within the season.
One month, three conferences and an exhibition, set in copper and sun with big condensed type.
“Une conférence sur les 30 ans du Mois de l'histoire des Noirs” — Instagram post 111. The 2026 season marks thirty years of Black History Month.

Titles, formats and venues as published in the season posts. Days are given without a month in the posts; the conference titles are set in capitals.

The conference series runs at Campus MIL at 18:00. Chantier brings ten artists, invited by Bousmaha Seddiki and Leonel Jules, to Galerie Art Mûr.
Vers un avenir plus juste et équitable
Sources: Instagram posts 109 and 111; Chantier posters.
The season is the first full use of the positioning proposed in A.A.A.’s brand audit. The audit marked where CCAM should move on four scales; the season should read from the right-hand column.
Source: “Positionnement actuel”, A.A.A. brand audit, slide 08.

The season title is MOIS DE L’HISTOIRE DES NOIRS, outlined from Animo Condensed and stacked one word per line, flush left.

Measured on the 1080 px post: cap height 199 px, line pitch about 220 px (a gap of roughly a tenth of the cap height), left edge on x = 92.

The CCAM logo closes the last line. It is set to the cap height (197 px) and bottom-aligned with NOIRS.

Where the outlined stack does not fit, set the title as live type: Animo Condensed 238.6 / 83% leading, −2% tracking, centred, on a 1080 px post.

The line breaks follow the measure, not one word per line. NOIRS falls on its own last line.

Every season post carries the label 2026 CALENDRIER in Inter Regular, Sun on Copper.

Measured: 32.3 px on post 104, top right and level with the top of the title; 27.4 px on post 105, centred above the title.

Keep the label small. It names the season; the title does the shouting.
Inter Regular, 0% tracking. Shown at 120 px and at the measured 32.3 px.

Event titles are set in capitals in Animo Condensed, sized to their column.

CHANTIER fills the full width of its column on every poster: 297.2 px across the 1007 px column of the 1920 poster, 528.1 px on the portrait poster and 683 px on the square.

Conference titles on the 1080 px posts: 95–100 px, 90–95% leading, 0 to −1% tracking.

Use the stacked CCAM logo in one flat colour: Copper on Sun or Sun on Copper.

Measured sizes: 44 × 70 px on information posts, 124 × 197 px when it closes the title stack, 99–103 px wide on posters.

It sits top right (80 px in, on the grid margin), bottom centre, or bottom right on posters (20–58 px from the edge).

— Don’t retype the title in another face.
— Don’t open up the tracking.
— Don’t loosen the leading.
— Don’t recolour outside Sun and Copper.
— Don’t set titles in sentence case.
— Don’t stretch or squash the type.

The season uses two colours and no others: Sun and Copper. One is always the ground and the other carries every word, rule and logo.

Use one yellow only. Sun is the same on screen and in print.

CMYK values are a direct conversion. Proof them on the paper stock before printing.

Copper and Sun have a contrast ratio of 3.9:1. That passes WCAG AA for large text only.

The smallest season text is 16.3 px on a 1080 px post, which shows at about a third of that size on a phone.

Recommended: keep running text at 24 px or more on a 1080 canvas, and short labels at 18 px or more.

Share of each surface across the nine unique season pieces, each piece weighted equally (6 posts, 3 poster formats).

The posts are Copper-led; the posters are Sun-led and give over half their area to the exhibition image.

Text and rules are not counted.

Two pairings.

Copper ground: posts 104, 105, 109, 111 and 112.

Sun ground: post 115 and every Chantier poster.

Alternate the two across a feed so the grid reads as a pattern rather than a block.

Animo Condensed Regular is the season’s display face, set in capitals for every title, date and event name.

The audit chose it as “franc et solide mais approchable”: frank and solid, but approachable.

Use one weight only, Regular. Do not use the Outline styles.

Measured sizes, by role and format. Posts are 1080 × 1350; posters are 1920 × 1080, 1835 × 2347 (portrait) and 2347 × 2347 (square).

When adding a format, scale from the nearest measured one.

Inter is the season’s text face: the season label, venues, times, descriptions and artist names.

Use Regular for names and labels, Medium for venues, formats and descriptions. Venues and times are set in capitals with slightly tightened tracking.

Measured Inter sizes. All are on the 1080 px posts except artist names, which keep 27.4 px on every poster format.

Date tags use three different settings across the posts; see 5.1.

Animo carries the title; Inter carries everything you read second.

— Title in Animo capitals, venue and time beneath or above it in Inter Medium capitals.
— A date tag sits to the left of or above the title.
— Descriptions in Inter Medium, sentence case, narrow measure (440 px on a 1080 post).

A date tag is the day number in a pill. It marks each event in a programme.

The posts use three versions. Recommended: standardise on the outline tag from posts 111 and 112 (78 × 44 px, 2 px Sun stroke, fully rounded, Inter Regular 26.8), and use the filled version only on a Sun ground.
Outline — posts 111, 112. 78 × 44, 2 px stroke, Inter Regular 26.8
Outline, small — post 109. 57 × 32, 2 px stroke, Inter Bold 19.6
Filled — post 115. 77 × 43, Copper fill, Animo Normal 26.4

Programme posts list events top to bottom, flush left on the 80 px margin. Each event is a block: date tag, title, venue and time, and an optional description.

Blocks are divided by 1 px Sun rules that run off both edges of the post.

The blocks may change height to suit the copy (posts 111 and 112), but the order inside each block does not change.

“VERS UN AVENIR PLUS JUSTE ET ÉQUITABLE”  “IMAGE OU RÉALITÉ”
Tie each event to the thirty years of Black History Month and to the people it honours.
“Une conférence sur les 30 ans du Mois de l'histoire des Noirs”
Venue and time on one line, with no preamble.
Name the artists and the curators in full, every time.
“10 ARTISTES INVITÉS PAR Bousmaha Seddiki Et LEONEL JULES”
Invite people; don’t summon them. The audit found the former brand had this relationship with its audience:
“Relation avec une autorité et non avec un pair.” — audit, slide 08

Short, concrete, warm. Write as a neighbour inviting someone in, not as an institution announcing.

Inconsistencies found in the season files. Settle these before the next round of material.

Suggested fixes are recommendations.
Artist names spelled differently: “Aniocles Grégoire” / “Anicole Gregoire”; “Shilov” / “Pascal smarth”
1920 and square posters vs portrait poster
Confirm the list with the curators and use one source everywhere
The 05 event has two titles: “Conférence-débat, 4e édition” and “Vers un avenir plus juste et équitable”
Pick one title, or set one as the subtitle
Mixed case hidden under all-caps styling: “FACe-À-FACE”, “Galerie arT mÛr”
Retype in normal case so copied and exported text reads correctly
Capitalisation in the credit line: “Bousmaha Seddiki Et LEONEL JULES”
Write “Bousmaha Seddiki et Leonel Jules” and let the style set the case
A hidden “2026” text layer sits below the frame of every post
Delete it, or bring it into the composition deliberately
